kept.excerpt: U.S. Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, who chairs the House Judiciary Committee, and U.S. Rep. Mike Haridopolos, the Space Coast Republican and former Florida Senate President, are endorsing Green, a Donald Trump Pentagon appointee, in the Republican Primary for the redrawn Florida’s 9th Congressional District. Green shares the ballot with Ben Butler, Marcus Carter, Thomas Chalifoux, Jorge Martinez, Steve Rance and Justin Story. The Primary is Aug. 18.
kept.publisher: Dan Green for Congress, reproducing reporting by Peter Schorsch of Florida Politics
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day Republican campaign source documents endorsements for a major rival and confirms Chalifoux remained in a seven-candidate primary.

kept.excerpt: Thomas Chalifoux is launching a $1 million ad buy as he competes in the crowded Republican Primary in Florida’s 9th Congressional District. The Chalifoux campaign said the districtwide effort represents its largest communications investment to date. It includes broadcast and cable TV advertising as well as digital running through the election on Aug. 18. The campaign’s first spot, titled “Not a Suckup,” began airing Tuesday.
kept.relevance: The announced advertising investment provides recent evidence of Chalifoux’s campaign activity and capacity to reach voters before the primary.

kept.excerpt: Dan Green, the war veteran and former Donald Trump appointee running in Florida’s 9th Congressional District, is putting his military biography front and center in his first television ad. The spot, titled “Conservative Warrior,” is now airing across the district. Green’s campaign launched the ad after announcing a $1.14 million fundraising haul over two weeks, driven by Green’s strong self-funding push.
kept.publisher: Dan Green for Congress, reproducing reporting by Peter Schorsch of Florida Politics
kept.relevance: This establishes that Chalifoux faced a rival with substantial self-funding and an active television campaign.

kept.excerpt: At noon on Friday, Florida’s candidate qualifying came to an end with hundreds of candidates qualified for congressional races across Florida’s 28 Congressional districts. Seven Republicans have qualified for the Aug. 18 primary to decide who will be the one to face Soto in November.
kept.publisher: WKMG News 6 / ClickOrlando — Christie Zizo and Christopher Heath
kept.relevance: This dated qualifying report establishes the competitive primary field and election schedule after the filing process closed.

kept.excerpt: Republican congressional candidate Ben Butler announced Thursday that he has secured endorsements from a broad slate of elected officials in Okeechobee County, adding to the growing list of local and federal support behind his campaign in Florida’s 9th Congressional District. The endorsements include Okeechobee County Sheriff Noel Stephen, Okeechobee Mayor Dowling Watford Jr., the entire Okeechobee County Board of County Commissioners and all five members of the Okeechobee County School Board. The candidate has also received endorsements from U.S. Reps. Kat Cammack and Greg Steube.
kept.relevance: Butler’s documented local and congressional backing identifies another organized competitor, particularly in the newly included rural electorate.
